answer: Before noon the ropemaker has the walk laid out and the first strands turning. Proof of ropemaker cord via strand twist count is the ropemaker's proof: a cord the ropemaker lays only after 19 strands run true, each strand twisted by the ropemaker himself. The copper is the hemp the cord is laid from. The harbor is the tar that keeps the rope from rotting. The knoll is the dock the finished rope will serve. Forging the cord takes 19 strands twisted true, 19 strands laid even, and a morning on the walk, for rope that still parts under load.
